quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, you should use both brakes:

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the strongest stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Motorcyclists riding in a group should not ride side-by-side because:

options.text: A driver merging may not see both riders.
Light bouncing off both helmets may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding side-by-side does not give riders enough space to move and avoid danger.
It is hard for riders on the left to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding side-by-side does not give riders enough space to move and avoid danger.
questions.explanation: In a group, motorcyclists should never ride side-by-side. Each rider needs enough room to move and avoid hazards.

questions.question: Goggles can:

options.text: Protect both your eyes and face.
Protect your face but not your eyes.
Protect your eyes but not your face.
Protect neither your face nor your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield is needed to protect your entire face during a crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Where do conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers happen most often?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers happen most often. Riders should be extra careful at intersections.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at a motorcyclist without noticing them.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is much stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: You should choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your safety cushion and makes you visible to others.
Increases your safety cushion and makes you visible to others.
Puts you near road hazards and allows others to share your lane.
Reduces road hazards but requires you to follow other vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your safety cushion and makes you visible to others.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that increases your safety cushion and helps others see you. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you room to escape danger. Maximize your safety cushion.

questions.question: When following another vehicle as a new rider, you should:

options.text: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Get as close as possible to the other vehicle.
Always ride on the left side of your lane so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: New riders should keep at least four seconds of following distance. Increase this distance if weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be:
questions.correctAnswerText: A speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other traffic rule signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Rain suits should:

options.text: Not be needed because motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not balloon when you ride.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits for motorcycles will not tear or balloon up when you ride at high speeds.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your crash risk, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing when riding to make yourself more visible to other drivers, even during the day.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you avoid blind spots, see and be seen, avoid road hazards, and gives you an escape route. You should position yourself to discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: Keeping a space cushion around you allows you to:

options.text: Maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: A space cushion gives you time to react and maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol after drinking?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. You cannot speed up this process. Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol in your body.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride on the left side of the lane.
Ride on the right side of the lane.
Move back and forth across the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: Which of the following will not protect a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and sturdy protective clothing to protect yourself while riding.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep the motorcycle upright. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: Making eye contact with other drivers:

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Does not mean they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know that a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still not notice you.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze the front brake hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit will help you stop quickly if you need to. It is easier to use both brakes in an emergency if you practice using them together.

questions.question: A proper lane position helps you do all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Your lane position is important for safety. It should help you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns you plan to make.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal, as it may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal your intention, check for traffic, and pass when safe. Then signal again and return to your original lane when you can.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.
